essence: Wave Warp remaps the layer by displacing pixels along a repeating wave field. Wave Height sets displacement amplitude, Wave Width sets the wave’s spacing, and Direction plus Wave Speed determine where the pattern travels over time; Wave Type changes the shape of that displacement.
manifests_as: The image bends into repeating bands, ripples, or angular wave-shaped offsets that can drift continuously across the frame.

key_levers.name: Wave Type
key_levers.effect: Selects the waveform used to calculate pixel displacement, changing the distortion from smooth rolling motion to sharper, more geometric, or noise-like motion.

key_levers.name: Wave Height
key_levers.effect: Controls the amplitude of pixel displacement: larger absolute values create stronger bends, while reversing the sign flips the displacement direction.

key_levers.name: Wave Width
key_levers.effect: Controls wave spacing: lower values pack more waves into the image, while higher values produce fewer, broader bends.

key_levers.name: Direction
key_levers.effect: Rotates the direction in which the wave pattern propagates, changing the orientation and travel path of the visible distortion.

key_levers.name: Wave Speed
key_levers.effect: Sets how quickly the wave field advances over time; zero freezes the pattern, and negative values make it travel in the opposite direction.

key_levers.name: Phase
key_levers.effect: Offsets the wave’s current position without changing its shape; animate it for manually timed wave travel or use it to align the pattern at a specific frame.

key_levers.name: Pinning
key_levers.effect: Chooses which layer edges resist displacement, preventing selected borders from visibly rippling or pulling away from their original positions.

enums_to_verify.Wave Type (ADBE Wave Warp-0001, 1-9): Unverified: value 1 is believed to be a sine-style smooth wave; remaining values are believed to select progressively different geometric and/or noise waveforms, but exact labels and ordering must be verified in this build.
enums_to_verify.Pinning (ADBE Wave Warp-0006, 1-11): Unverified: values are believed to represent no pinning plus combinations of pinned layer edges/corners; exact edge mappings and ordering must be verified in this build.
enums_to_verify.Antialiasing (Best Quality) (ADBE Wave W: Unverified: values are believed to select increasing edge-smoothing quality levels, with a render-speed versus smoothness tradeoff.

config_recipes.subtle water shimmer: Wave Type 1, Wave Height 8, Wave Width 120%, Direction 90 degrees, Wave Speed 0.35, Phase 0 degrees; use no/low edge pinning unless the layer boundary must stay still.
config_recipes.broad rolling fabric: Wave Type 1, Wave Height 25, Wave Width 220%, Direction 0 degrees, Wave Speed 0.7; pin the attachment edge if the fabric must appear fixed there.
config_recipes.aggressive heat-wave distortion: Use a smooth or noise-like Wave Type after verification, Wave Height 18, Wave Width 55%, Direction 90 degrees, Wave Speed 1.5; reduce height if fine image detail becomes unreadable.
config_recipes.frozen ripple texture: Wave Type 1, Wave Height 16, Wave Width 70%, Direction 45 degrees, Wave Speed 0, Phase 30 degrees; animate Phase only if the still pattern later needs timed movement.

reasoning_hooks: Wave Height is the primary intensity lever; increasing Wave Speed only makes the same distortion move faster and does not make it stronger.
Wave Width and Wave Height interact perceptually: a large height with a narrow width creates tightly folded, harsh distortion, while the same height with a wide width reads as broad rolling motion.
At Wave Speed 0, the effect can still be fully visible, but it reads as a static warped image rather than a wave animation.
Direction controls propagation orientation, not merely a decorative rotation; change it before judging whether the wave motion is traveling the intended way.
Use Pinning when a warped layer’s boundary must remain attached to another element; otherwise edge movement can expose transparent borders or create unwanted seam motion.
Phase is best for timing or offsetting the existing pattern; it does not change wave amplitude or spacing.
